engine_rules.name: Note Density Decoupled from Musical Value
engine_rules.preference: Prefer rhythmic awareness and variety over maximizing note count per bar
engine_rules.falsifier: A passage that equates denser note-filling with superior improvisation
engine_rules.anchor: More notes per bar is not better than a few, just different.

engine_rules.name: Rhythmic Awareness as Primary Goal
engine_rules.preference: Track which rhythms are in use and bar-position at all times
engine_rules.falsifier: Improvisation that ignores bar position
engine_rules.anchor: your awareness of where you are in the bar

engine_rules.name: Note Grouping Bar-Line Independence
engine_rules.preference: Play fixed-count groupings without anchoring start or end to bar lines
engine_rules.falsifier: A grouping that always begins and ends on beat one
engine_rules.anchor: play them independent of bar lines

engine_rules.name: Mental Grouping Drives Articulation
engine_rules.preference: Conceive notes in explicit groupings even when groupings overlap or are invisible to listeners
engine_rules.falsifier: Playing without internal grouping conception that produces undifferentiated articulation
engine_rules.anchor: How I'm thinking about these groupings of notes will effect the articulation of the lines.

engine_rules.name: Five-Note Grouping as Polyrhythm Entry Point
engine_rules.preference: Use five-note eighth-note groupings to begin hearing polyrhythmic cross-rhythms
engine_rules.falsifier: Five-note groupings used only without polyrhythmic awareness
engine_rules.anchor: begin hearing polyrhythms. For example, take a five-note grouping

engine_rules.name: Five-Note Group Duration Flexibility
engine_rules.preference: Play five consecutive notes occupying 1, 1.5, 2, 3, or 4 beats
engine_rules.falsifier: Five-note group always played at one fixed duration
engine_rules.anchor: The five notes can be played as 1 beat or 1 1/2 beats. 2 beats, 3 beats, or + beats, etc.

engine_rules.name: 22-Rhythm Palette Excludes Sixteenth Notes and Triplets
engine_rules.preference: Use only quarter notes and eighth notes in the 22 one-bar rhythms; defer sixteenth notes and triplets
engine_rules.falsifier: Sixteenth note or triplet used within the 22-rhythm chapter exercise set
engine_rules.anchor: Sixteenth notes and triplets have been purposely omitted at this point.

engine_rules.name: 22 Rhythms Practiced as Embodied Physical Feel
engine_rules.preference: Feel each rhythm inside the body as a rhythm instrument would
engine_rules.falsifier: Rhythm practiced purely intellectually without physical internalization
engine_rules.anchor: feel the rhythm inside your body

engine_rules.name: Rhythmic Displacement by Whole-Beat Offsets
engine_rules.preference: Systematically play each of the 22 rhythms one beat early, two beats early, and one beat late
engine_rules.falsifier: Rhythm always played at its notated position without displacement
engine_rules.anchor: you can play each rhythm one beat early, or two beats early, or one beat late

engine_rules.name: Half-Beat Displacement Produces Perceptually Distinct Rhythms
engine_rules.preference: Use half-beat offsets (1/2, 1 1/2, 2 1/2 beats) to generate new rhythmic identities from existing patterns
engine_rules.falsifier: Half-beat displacement treated as a mere timing shift without perceptual effect
engine_rules.anchor: displacing a rhythm 1/2 of a beat, or 1 1/2 beats, or 2 1/2 beats, you create entirely different sounding rhythms at times.

engine_rules.name: Four Consecutive Eighth Notes Displaced Across Eight Entry Points
engine_rules.preference: Begin with beat 1 entry, then systematically start on each of the eight eighth-note positions in the bar
engine_rules.falsifier: Skipping any of the eight entry points before randomization
engine_rules.anchor: displace the grouping by starting on eight different place#in the bar.

engine_rules.name: Harmony Anticipation at Eighth-Note Entry Points 6-8
engine_rules.preference: At positions 6, 7, 8, approach the next chord or state it directly
engine_rules.falsifier: Late entry positions that resolve only to the current chord
engine_rules.anchor: For #6, #7, and #8, the harmony can be anticipated.

engine_rules.name: Final Eighth Note Sounds Next Chord at Displacement 5
engine_rules.preference: At displacement position 5, let the final eighth note sound a tone of the next chord
engine_rules.falsifier: Position 5 ending on current-chord tone rather than next-chord tone
engine_rules.anchor: On this rhythm the last eighth note would sound the next chord.

engine_rules.name: Combine One-Bar Rhythms into Multi-Bar Phrases
engine_rules.preference: Combine two, three, and four one-bar rhythms and play through a tune
engine_rules.falsifier: Practicing only isolated one-bar patterns after mastering individual displacement
engine_rules.anchor: Combine two of the one-bar rhythms. Create a two-bar rhythm and play it through a tune.

engine_rules.name: 3/4-over-4/4 Metric Superimposition
engine_rules.preference: Play a four-note grouping continuously to create felt 3/4 over 4/4; note the three-bar resolution cycle
engine_rules.falsifier: Three-note grouping assumed to be 3/4 superimposition without tracking resolution cycle
engine_rules.anchor: This is a 3/4 pattern which takes three bars of 4/4 to work out.

engine_rules.name: Randomize Entry Points After Ordered Drilling
engine_rules.preference: After completing all eight ordered positions, mix starting beats randomly
engine_rules.falsifier: Randomization used before completing ordered position drilling
engine_rules.anchor: Try playing four consecutive eighth notes on different beats randomly

engine_rules.name: Five Consecutive Eighth Notes Across All Eight Entry Points
engine_rules.preference: Drill five consecutive eighth notes starting on each of the eight eighth-note positions in the bar using Tunes 1, 2, 3
engine_rules.falsifier: Skipping any entry point before moving to randomization
engine_rules.anchor: practice playing five consecutive eighth notes beginning on these eight

engine_rules.name: Five-Note Bar-Cross Harmony Anticipation at Positions 5-7
engine_rules.preference: When five-note groups cross the bar line at positions 5-7, anticipate the next chord
engine_rules.falsifier: Bar-crossing five-note group at position 5-7 that ignores next-chord anticipation
engine_rules.anchor: For #5, #6, and #7, the eighth notes before crossing the bar line can either anticipate the next

engine_rules.name: Mix Five-Note Entry Points After Systematic Drilling
engine_rules.preference: After mastering steps 1-8 in order, mix starting points freely and randomly
engine_rules.falsifier: Random practice before completing all eight ordered positions
engine_rules.anchor: Start five consecutive eighth notes on different beats randomly

engine_rules.name: Entry-Point Drilling Opens Window for Form Awareness
engine_rules.preference: Practice systematic entry-point displacement as means to internalize perception of larger time spans and form
engine_rules.falsifier: Displacement practice treated as purely mechanical with no perceptual goal
engine_rules.anchor: Practicing with these devices opens up a window in the part of the mind that hears bigger

engine_rules.name: 3/4-over-4/4 Starting on Upbeat
engine_rules.preference: Initiate 3/4 superimposition on the 'and' of beat rather than on beat 1 for additional textural variety
engine_rules.falsifier: 3/4 superimposition always anchored to beat 1
engine_rules.anchor: another 3/4 pattern over 4/4 which starts on the "and" of beat

engine_rules.name: 7/4-over-4/4 Metric Superimposition
engine_rules.preference: Sustain a seven-beat phrase pattern over 4/4 for the full eight-bar resolution cycle
engine_rules.falsifier: Seven-beat grouping abandoned before the eight-bar resolution point
engine_rules.anchor: Here is a 7/4 pattern over 4/4.

engine_rules.name: 9/4-over-4/4 Metric Superimposition
engine_rules.preference: Sustain a nine-beat phrase pattern over 4/4
engine_rules.anchor: Here is a 9/4 pattern over 4/4,

engine_rules.name: 5/4-over-4/4 Metric Superimposition Aligning on Bar 6
engine_rules.preference: Play five-beat pattern over 4/4 for full cycle; note that the pattern returns to beat 1 on the sixth bar
engine_rules.falsifier: 5/4 pattern abandoned before six-bar resolution cycle completes
engine_rules.anchor: This is a 5/4 pattern over 4/4.

engine_rules.name: Three Harmonic Roles for Late-Position Seven-Note Groups
engine_rules.preference: At late entry positions (beat 3 through and-of-4), choose from: anticipate next chord, approach it via passing tones, or sound current chord
engine_rules.falsifier: Late entry positions restricted to only one harmonic role
engine_rules.anchor: these eighth notes can anticipate the next chord, or they can be approach notes to the next chord, or they can sound the chord of the moment.

engine_rules.name: Close Pedagogical Loop: Apply Superimposition to Random Starts
engine_rules.preference: After drilling polymetric patterns 10-14, return to exercise 9 (random starts) and apply the superimposition techniques within it
engine_rules.falsifier: Superimposition exercises never integrated back into free random-start playing
engine_rules.anchor:
After practicing #10-14 go back and try #9 again using

some of these time signature devices.

engine_rules.name: Randomize Seven-Note Entry Points After Ordered Drill
engine_rules.preference: After mastering all ordered entry points for seven-note groups, mix starting beats randomly
engine_rules.falsifier: Random starts before completing all eight ordered positions
engine_rules.anchor: Try starting six consecutive eighth notes form different beats randomly, for example:

engine_rules.name: Eight Metrical Entry Positions as Displacement Grid
engine_rules.preference: Define eight starting positions as the complete set of metrical entry points for all consecutive-note displacement work
engine_rules.falsifier: Fewer than eight positions treated as the full set
engine_rules.anchor:
1. Starting on beat one.

2. Starting on the "and" of beat one.

3. Starting on beat two.

4. Starting on the "and" of beat two.

engine_rules.name: 11/4-over-4/4 Asymmetric Metric Superimposition
engine_rules.preference: Sustain an eleven-beat pattern over 4/4 as an advanced cross-rhythm device
engine_rules.anchor: This is an 11/4 pattern over 4/4.

engine_rules.name: 6/4-over-4/4 Metric Superimposition
engine_rules.preference: Sustain a six-beat pattern over 4/4
engine_rules.anchor: This is a 6/4 pattern over 4/4.

engine_rules.name: Integrate Polyrhythms Back Into Random-Start Free Play
engine_rules.preference: After exercises 10-14, return to random-start exercise 9 deploying time-signature devices spontaneously
engine_rules.falsifier: Polyrhythm exercises never fed back into free-start context
engine_rules.anchor: After practicing #10-14 go back and try #9 again using some of these time signature devices,

engine_rules.name: Three Consecutive Triplet Groupings Displaced Across Bar
engine_rules.preference: Practice three consecutive eighth-note triplets starting from different positions within the bar using the same eight-position grid
engine_rules.falsifier: Triplet displacement restricted to downbeat starts
engine_rules.anchor:
practice playing groupings of three consecutive eighth notes starting on
different places within the bar.

engine_rules.name: Odd-Meter Triplet Superimposition over 4/4 Pulse
engine_rules.preference: Notate in odd time signatures but always feel and play as superimposition over 4/4
engine_rules.falsifier: Odd-meter exercises played by actually changing felt meter rather than superimposing
engine_rules.anchor:
The following exercises, 10-13, are written out in varying time signatures but should be played
superimposed over

engine_rules.name: Sound Four of Six Triplet Subdivisions
engine_rules.preference: Across two consecutive triplet groups (six total subdivisions), sound only four; let two remain silent
engine_rules.falsifier: All six triplet subdivisions sounded, eliminating the rhythmic texture of selective silencing
engine_rules.anchor: only four of the six notes are sounded.

engine_rules.name: Melodic Displacement to Internalize Triplet Groupings
engine_rules.preference: Play the same short melody starting on each entry point to get used to the feel of triplet displacement
engine_rules.falsifier: Melodic displacement skipped in favor of only abstract rhythmic drilling
engine_rules.anchor:
try playing the same four-note melody starting on the differ-

ent beats

engine_rules.name: Randomize Triplet Groupings After Structured Drill
engine_rules.preference: After completing all ordered positions for triplet groupings, mix them randomly
engine_rules.falsifier: Random triplet groupings used before completing ordered position drilling
engine_rules.anchor: 16, Practice plaving these preceding triplet groupings randomly.

engine_rules.name: 7/4-over-4/4 Triplet Phrase Superimposition
engine_rules.preference: Sustain a seven-unit triplet phrase over 4/4 for the full resolution cycle
engine_rules.anchor: Try this 7/4 rhythm over 4/4.

engine_rules.name: Randomize Six-Triplet Groupings for Free Improvisation
engine_rules.preference: After ordered drilling, practice six consecutive triplets starting randomly
engine_rules.falsifier: Random triplet starts used before completing the ordered drill
engine_rules.anchor: Practice playing six consecutive eighth-note triplets randomly.

engine_rules.name: Randomize Seven-Consecutive-Triplet Starts
engine_rules.preference: After mastering ordered positions for seven triplets, mix starts freely
engine_rules.falsifier: Random starts used before completing ordered triplet drilling
engine_rules.anchor: 15. Practice playing seven consecutive eighth-note triplets randomly.

engine_rules.name: 5/4-over-4/4 Triplet Superimposition
engine_rules.preference: Sustain a five-unit triplet phrase over 4/4 for full resolution cycle
engine_rules.anchor: 1+. Try this 5/4 rhythm over 4/4.
